data.body:
Phase 2 complete — fix pushed as Gerrit change 2072 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2072).

TEST (RED->GREEN, held out): tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding_isolation.py. It drives the polluter's real teardown path and asserts sys.modules['rebar._store.ensures'] is rebar._store.ensures. Confirmed legitimately RED first (two distinct module objects from the same file), then held out of the fix subagent's working tree entirely — moved out of the repo, not merely omitted from the prompt — so the GREEN was earned against an oracle the fixer never saw.

MUTATION CHECK (the test has teeth): deleting the single restoring line (setattr(parent, attr, restored)) returns BOTH the new oracle AND the original reported symptom to RED (assert ['run'] == ['ensures','run']). Restored afterwards.

FIX: tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding.py — the hand-rolled sys.modules-only save/restore is replaced with a _reimportable(name) context manager that snapshots the parent package and the sys.modules entry on enter and restores BOTH in a finally (so it survives a raising body). The d720-fc72 capture window the test exists to reproduce is preserved: temporarily reverting src/rebar/_store/ensures.py to a by-value 'from rebar._store.lock import canonical_tracker' still makes it fail as designed.

HARDENING at the victim site: test_mcp_startup_sweeps_before_run now asserts its module-identity precondition before monkeypatching. Verified this fires — under the mutated (leaky) teardown the failure is now 'rebar._store.ensures diverges from the collection-time binding: an earlier test re-imported the module and restored sys.modules but not the package attribute' instead of the baffling assert ['run'] == ['ensures','run'].

NO PRODUCTION CHANGE. The isdir(tracker_dir()) guard in mcp_server.main() is not implicated — the runtime probe showed it resolving correctly and returning True — so there is no user-facing 'MCP server started from another directory silently skips its sweep' bug here. src/rebar/ is untouched; the whole diff is 3 test files.

SIBLING SWEEP:
- Construct axis (pop-a-submodule-from-sys.modules + a genuine fresh importlib import inside the window — the only signature that rebinds a parent attribute): ONE instance in the suite, the one fixed. Cleared: tests/unit/test_capabilities.py uses importlib.reload (mutates in place, same object); every monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, ...) site installs a stub, and 'import X.Y' short-circuits on a present sys.modules entry so no parent rebind occurs; tests/unit/conftest.py seeds a top-level shadow package once without swap-and-restore.
- Parity axis: N/A — a test-local re-import dance has no CLI/MCP/library surface parity dimension.

RESIDUAL RISK: tests/conftest.py::block_extra evicts submodules and restores sys.modules only, i.e. the same shape — but it BLOCKS imports during its window, so no successful fresh load can rebind a parent attribute, and sys.modules is restored before any import can succeed. Latent, not live. Disposition: accepted, no ticket.

REPLICATION: the original report no longer reproduces in either order. 70 passed across every ensures-touching test (tests/unit/test_ensures_late_binding{,_isolation,_untrack_markers,_boot_budget_e43f}.py, test_init_ensures_seam.py, tests/interfaces/store/{test_fsck_ensures,test_ensures,test_ensure_invariants,test_pending_hint}.py).

GATES: make lint OK; make typecheck OK (625 files); complexity ratchet active=46 new=0 increased=0 (stale=3, pre-existing).

NOTE FOR THE CLOSE: caused_by is already linked to d720-fc72-3763-4cac; still pass --caused-by=d720-fc72-3763-4cac --class=regression on the close so blame auto-derivation does not add a competing guessed edge. Worth recording: d720-fc72 was ITSELF an ordering-pollution bug, and its fix introduced a new ordering pollution of the same class.
